entries.6b61223924b35ee6: The annual securities report states that accommodation sales are easily affected by economic conditions and trends in personal consumption, and that a decline in individual and corporate guests could affect results. Key management indicators include the number of guests, room occupancy rate, operating profit, and the growth rates of these indicators. Also, the company concentrates transactions for food ingredients in its food and beverage division with specific suppliers. The company purchases processed foods, meat, vegetables and other items from Toho Food Service Co., Ltd., with purchases of ¥1,197 million in the fiscal year ended November 2025, equal to 46% of food ingredient purchases. Ingredients for Joyfull stores are purchased from Joyfull Co., Ltd., with purchases of ¥248 million, equal to 10% of food ingredient purchases.
entries.6cb9eb935dd232c4: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the company mainly operates hotel facilities for accommodation and provides restaurant and other food and beverage services attached to them, and that it operates "HOTEL AZ" mainly in the Kyushu region. The business involves opening outlets along arterial roads (roadside) or near small and medium-sized stations, in areas with few other hotels, rather than near terminal stations or entertainment and dining districts, and offering systemized and standardized services at affordable prices to win the support of users. As of November 30, 2025, there were 91 HOTEL AZ outlets (88 company-operated and three franchised). Revenue for the fiscal year ended November 2025 was ¥19,560 million (the previous fiscal year was ¥18,029 million). The company does not prepare consolidated financial statements, so all figures are those of the company on a non-consolidated basis.

entries.7d457ad31b592623: Rather than offering banquet and premium dining functions like general city hotels, or providing room service with sufficient staff, the company offers uniform, adequate service at reasonable prices. Many of its hotel stores have attached family restaurants: in addition to its own original stores, the company operates ‘Shabushabu Onyasai’ and ‘Kamadoka’ as a franchisee of Nisul Co., Ltd., and ‘Joyfull’ as a franchisee of Joyfull Co., Ltd. As a growth strategy, the annual securities report states that the company is developing a new HOTEL AZ series with 158-room types and will expand stores in the Chugoku and Shikoku regions.

entries.b1c229d4b8932fff: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended November 2025 was ¥3,199 million (¥3,760 million in the previous fiscal year), ordinary profit was ¥2,842 million (¥3,405 million), and net income was ¥2,081 million (¥2,236 million), as revenue increased while profit decreased. The annual securities report states that although revenue increased, cost of sales rose to ¥2,607 million (¥2,298 million) due to soaring raw material prices, and selling, general and administrative expenses rose to ¥13,754 million (¥11,970 million) due to the costs of four new stores, higher personnel costs from raising salary levels, and increases in outsourcing fees, linen costs, utility costs and others. The company plans to fund capital expenditure for new stores mainly through borrowings from financial institutions; as of November 30, 2025, interest-bearing debt (including lease obligations) accounted for 38% of total assets.

entries.bbe1d2cd187f179f: Revenue for the fiscal year ended November 2025 was ¥19,560 million (¥18,029 million in the previous fiscal year). The breakdown is: accommodation division ¥14,245 million, food and beverage division ¥4,556 million, other ¥302 million, and off-site food and beverage business ¥456 million. The annual securities report states that the reasons for the revenue increase were solid accommodation use due to the effects of the dominant strategy and online sales strengthening measures, higher average spend per customer in the second half due to the price revision in June, and four new store openings.

entries.fe125918206c0e20: A business that operates the accommodation-focused business hotel "HOTEL AZ" along suburban arterial roads and similar locations, and also runs restaurants attached to the hotels; it is the only category the securities report lists as a reportable segment. As of November 30, 2025, it operates 91 HOTEL AZ locations (88 directly operated, 3 franchised). Net sales for the fiscal year ended November 2025 (total of reportable segments) were ¥19,104 million (108.7% of the same period of the previous year). The securities report cites the effect of the dominant strategy and measures to strengthen online sales as having kept accommodation use solid, the June price revision as having raised the average spend per guest in the second half, and the opening of 4 new locations as reasons for the increase in sales. Because there is only one reportable segment, segment profit is not stated.
entries.ff2451ff230274d9: The division of family restaurants and similar establishments attached to HOTEL AZ locations. In addition to the Company's original restaurants, it operates "Shabu-shabu Onyasai" and "Kamadoka" as a franchisee of Nisul Co., Ltd., and "Joyfull" as a franchisee of Joyfull Co., Ltd. Net sales for the fiscal year ended November 2025 were ¥4,556 million (113.2% of the same period of the previous year).
